subject: Transient custody & expedited return / deletion — order form Q&A
messages:
From: Erik Solis <erik.solis@novamed.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novamed Legal <legal@novamed.com>
Date: 2027-05-26T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Transient custody question — 48h retention & proof of deletion

Hannah —

Quick question as we finalize the order form: for a subset of our workloads (de-identified telemetry for the trial cohort) we need an accelerated retention window. Can Redwood commit to a T+48h maximum residency (where T = ingestion) for ephemeral telemetry, with an accelerated deletion timeline for cached KV and prefix caches? Specifically:

- Primary requirement: all "ephemeral telemetry" must be fully deleted from active serving nodes within 48 hours of ingestion.
- Secondary: backups and snapshots can be removed within T+7 days but must never be copied to long-term storage.
- We also need a deletion attestation/certificate (signed) showing the deletion events and checksum of wiped segments for our audit.

Is this something that can be put in an order-form addendum / SLA clause? If yes, please indicate any operational caveats (cost, minimum commit, or hardware-level wipe requirements).

Thanks,
Erik
Erik Solis
Head of Platform Security — Novamed

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Erik Solis <erik.solis@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-26T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Transient custody question — 48h retention & proof of deletion

Erik — thanks for the clear specs. Short answer: yes, we can support an accelerated, per-data-stream retention profile, but there are trade-offs and a small set of order-form items we need to lock down. High-level notes below; attaching a draft order-form addendum and our deletion playbook for reference.

1) What we can guarantee
- Active-serving cache eviction & KV clearance within T+48h for tagged streams when customer chooses the "ephemeral" residency class.
- Snapshot/s3 lifecycle: snapshot copies held only for up to T+7 days and not delegated to archival tiers.
- Deletion logs: we can provide a machine-readable deletion event log (timestamps, object ids, node ids) and a signed deletion certificate.

2) Caveats / operational items
- For Dedicated & Private deployments we can provide hardware-anchored wipes on request. For Hosted customers we perform logical zeroization and secure overwrite; we do not physically decommission GPUs per deletion event (this would be a separate scope + cost).
- Expedited deletion below our standard SLO (we currently target 72h for general removal) will carry a one-time configuration fee and a sustained pricing uplift if you require guaranteed sub-48h across peak load windows.
- Extremely short windows increase the chance of transient request failures for long-running sessions — we recommend pinning sessions or using an "ephemeral-only" routing policy.

3) Suggested order-form language (draft excerpt)
"""
Section 4.7 (Ephemeral Residency Addendum)
Redwood will classify data streams labeled by Customer as "Ephemeral". For Ephemeral data: Redwood shall ensure logical deletion of active-serving cache entries and KV storage within forty-eight (48) hours of ingestion (T+48h). Snapshot retention of Ephemeral data shall not exceed seven (7) days (T+7). Redwood will provide a Deletion Certificate within ten (10) business days of a deletion event, which will include event timestamps, object identifiers, and a signed integrity checksum.
Operational exclusions: hardware-level physical destruction is out-of-scope unless separately procured.
"""

Next steps: Marissa — can you confirm order-form change and pricing impact? Neha — can you loop in infra on the signed-checksum feasibility? Erik — if that draft works for Novamed, we will convert to a change order and attach it to the existing PO.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0186

Attachments: novamed-orderform-draft.pdf, redwood-deletion-playbook-v2.md

From: Erik Solis <erik.solis@novamed.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novamed Legal <legal@novamed.com>
Date: 2027-05-28T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Transient custody question — 48h retention & proof of deletion

Hannah — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from Legal and our platform team:

- Certificate cadence: our auditors want certificates for monthly scrubs and on-demand for bulk deletion requests. Can Redwood produce both (monthly push + on-demand)?
- Integrity checksum format: can you confirm SHA-256 or equivalent? We need an immutable assertion we can store on our side.
- Chain-of-custody: for the playbook, do you track which containers/nodes handled a given object before deletion? The audit will want a mapping back to the ingestion session ID.

Also, Legal asked whether the T+48 and T+7 numbers can be expressed as maxima in the SLA (i.e., "no later than 48 hours"), not typical averages, and whether failure to meet these maxima triggers a service credit. We're okay with a credit ladder for SLA misses.

Would you and your infra folks be able to join a 30-minute call this week to walk through implementation details?

Erik

Subject: Re: Transient custody question — 48h retention & proof of deletion

Erik — appreciate the detailed follow-ups. Confirmations & commitments below, plus next steps to finalize the change order.

1) Certificates & cadence
- We can provide both scheduled monthly deletion attestations (pushed to the HubSpot/Drive link) and on-demand deletion certificates within ten (10) business days of a request.

2) Checksum & format
- We will provide SHA-256 checksums for deleted objects and include a signed manifest (PKCS7) that references the object IDs and node identifiers. The manifest will be downloadable and verifiable by your auditors.

3) Chain-of-custody
- Our deletion event log includes object ids, ingestion session id (when provided by the customer), node/container id, and timestamp. We will map ingestion session id -> object id as long as Novamed includes session metadata at ingestion (we'll add guidance to the playbook).

4) SLA maxima & credits
- We can express T+48 and T+7 as maxima in the addendum. Failure to meet maxima will trigger a service credit schedule. Sample: Miss window by >24h = 5% credit of monthly usage for that stream tier; >72h = 15% credit, escalates to formal remediation for repeated misses. Exact percentages to be finalized by Sales/Finance.

5) Implementation/cost notes
- Sub-48h guaranteed across peak load requires a Reserved-Ephemeral tier (minimum 1x reserved pool) and an expedited-delete configuration fee (one-time). We'll outline numbers in the order-form.

Call: Marissa and Neha are available Friday 2027-06-01 10:00-10:30 PT — does that work for you and Legal? If yes, we'll send a calendar invite and a draft change order for signature.

Regards,
Hannah
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
